header_sentences: See As, Free, Himself, Lead, Life, Love of self, and Proprium.

contexts.text: The goods he (now) produces are inanimate, because he supposes [that they are] from self. AC 29, Explained. AC 39.
Those in love... perceive that... they have not a whit of love, life, and happiness from themselves.
For man, from himself, is dead.
Want to enter into the mysteries of faith from themselves.
At first man produces as if from himself.

It is the least of all seeds, because the man supposes that he does good from himself. What is from self is nothing but evil; but, as he is in a state of regeneration, there is something of good, but the least of all.
[The celestial man] is not allowed (to know what is good and true) from self and the world. AC 126.
No one can do what is good from self.
That he desired to be led by self and the world. Signified.
Evil Spirits (are thus compelled to) confess that they do not live from themselves.
Of myself I do not think the least thing. From experience.
By believing that he lives from himself, man appropriates all evil and falsity. AC 4151:6. AC 4319. AC 6324. HH 547.
When Angels do not reflect, they know not but that they live from themselves.
Without the acknowledgement of self no one can be led to Heaven.
Not to eat of that tree = not to think of the good and truth of faith from themselves...
To be as God = that if they did so from themselves... they could lead themselves.
Man, of himself, cannot but do evil... yet the man does not do it... but still he is to blame. Explained.
Those who want to be innocent from themselves. Representation.
Such is the state of those who believe that they are spiritual from themselves, or that they can have faith from themselves.

Angelic Spirits made a beautiful candelabrum, as they supposed from themselves... I told them that they had invented and formed nothing from themselves... Being then illustrated, they confessed it was so. SE 2646.
Direful persuasions about the greatness of self. Treated of.
If he believes in simplicity that he can do good from himself...

At least they suppose that they do good and think truth from themselves... and the Lord leaves them so to think... But whatever man produces from self cannot be good, because it is from self, which is an impure fount... for he is always thinking about the merit and righteousness of self.
Whatever good a man supposes he does from self, returns to him; for it regards himself. (Signified by the return of the dove to Noah.) AC 882, Explained.
Man (supposes) that he thinks from himself; but has not the least of an idea from himself...
Man, from himself, is in Hell. AC 1049.
Said they could adore the Lord, but from themselves.
Humiliation consists in the acknowledgement of self: that with self there is nothing alive, or good... AC 2327:2. AC 2694:end.
How self is substituted for the Lord.
The sphere of one who regards himself in everything, appropriates everything to himself... thus all the delight of the Spirits around...
As there is present a continual reflection upon self...
Their very end being the worship of self... they acknowledge truth only so far as self is in it. AC 1322:2. AC 1326:4.
They perceive what is from the Lord, and what from self. Explained. AC 2882:end.
So long as Spirits suppose that they lead themselves, that they think from themselves, and know, understand, and are wise from themselves, they cannot have perception.
The sphere of one who has formed (a high) opinion of himself... Wherever he goes, looks at others, and speaks with them, he has an intuition of self... This forms a sphere. AC 1506, Example AC 1507.
(Holiness with the Angels dwells in the acknowledgement) that they know nothing from themselves.

At first, every man... attributes to himself (the good and truth from which he combats), and also the power... This is permitted... Before regeneration, no one can know... that nothing of good and truth is from himself... The Lord supposed the same.
Man must do good as from himself. SE 2733.
(Although) man does not live of himself, unless he appeared as if he lived from himself, he could not live at all.
They were dispersed of themselves.
When (the life of the internal man) inflows into affections which have self for their end... there results corporeal life.
If his end is self and the world, let him know that his life is infernal.
No one can look into himself; there must be something higher...
As they exhale a filthy idea of self, their delight is turned into a cadaverous stench, by which they are sensible of the Hell of self.
From himself, man does, thinks, and intends nothing but evil; and, from himself, rushes to Hell. AC 2410:2.
They who strive to do good from themselves, because the Lord has so commanded, are those who at last receive this good... They are then averse to the merit of self.
Man does not live from self, does not do good from self, does not believe truth from self, does not think from self... and, what is more, those in Hell do not think from self...
When there is anxiety (even to despair) because they can do nothing from themselves, the Persuasive is broken.
When they... perceive Hell in themselves...
The Divine Providence lest man should enter into the mysteries from self. Signified.
(Argument from man's not doing good from himself.)
So far as it is from themselves, the Angels are not in happiness.
The reason it is given to man to suppose that (good and truth) are from himself, is that they may become as his Own.

No man, Spirit, or Angel can will and think from himself, but from others; nor these others from themselves, but from others again, and so on; thus everyone from the Lord. AC 4319. AC 5986, From experience.
(Man not a machine, although he does not act from himself.)
By all means men ought to think, will, and do good from themselves.
He who believes that he rules himself is continually disquieted, is carried into cupidities... and causes (evils and falsities) to adhere to him.
Not to want to be redeemed by the Lord, but by themselves. Signified, Explained.

At first... all believe that they are reformed by themselves... and are left in this state by the Lord; for otherwise they cannot be reformed; for if they were told (then) that they cannot do anything of good of themselves, nor think anything of truth of themselves... they would await an influx... Or they would suppose that nothing is imputed to them justly. Or that they were like machines... and therefore it is granted them to think, at that time, that what is good and true is from themselves. AC 2960. AC 4145:2. AC 4151:3.
The spiritual are introduced through truth into good; but not into any will of good from themselves; because (this) has been destroyed with them.
Truth is given gratis, so as not to be from self. Signified.
An Angel has power from the Lord in proportion as he believes he has none from self.
As with a man who is in opposition in himself... he sees what is of the internal maia as opposed to himself...
He who acts from this precept... begins from himself, and... thinks of merit.
If man studies the neighbour and the Lord more than self, he is in a state of regeneration; but if he studies self more... he is not.
Privation of the life of truth from self. Signified, Explained. AC 3610.
(By hereditary evil) man, as to what is from himself, is nothing but evil... and, of himself, wills nothing of good...
Loving self above others... studying for self alone, and not for others except for the sake of self... he calls goods...
Such ideas are (first) insinuated as are not quite contrary to those he has had: as that all love begins from self; that self is first to be regarded, and then others...
Are indignant when told that they do not live from themselves.
Good cannot be appropriated to them, because they believe it is from themselves.

These loves have self for the end, which end kindles natural lumen, but extinguishes heavenly light; so that they see acutely the things of self and the world, but not a whit those of the Lord and His Kingdom...
If affections of truth and good are for the sake of self and the world, they are not genuine...

Sometimes it appears as if his ends were for self, when yet they are not; for man is such that in everything he reflects upon self... Let a man attend to the delight he perceives in himself from the praise and glory of self, and to that... from use separate from self. (This will show whether he is in genuine affection.)
Good becomes no good when reward is thought of; for an end for the sake of self at once adjoins itself, (which) induces denial that it is from the Lord... and thus removes the influx...

Faith from self, or from man's proprium, is not faith; for it causes falsities to be seen as truths, and truths as falsities; and, if the man sees truths as truths, still he does not see them, because he does not believe; for he sees himself in them, and not the Lord.
Under Cherub, see this reference.

Has (then) a perception that good from proprium must regard self, thus the preference of self before others, consequently contempt for others, and a feeling of merit. (External and internal truth) cannot be conjoined until the intuition of self begins to cease, and the intuition of the neighbour begins to be felt.
The natural man regards self and the world; but the spiritual man does not regard self and the world, except so far as conduces to promote uses in the Spiritual World.
For man to become spiritual... ends for self and the world must be put off...
Man believes that he is, and that from himself; when yet he is not from himself; but comes forth...
When anyone does good, not from the good of truth, he always wants to be recompensed; for he does it for the sake of self.

The proprium of innocence is that he knows, acknowledges, and believes, with the heart, that nothing but evil is from self... Then the Lord inflows with good and truth, and insinuates into him a heavenly proprium... He is then in the annihilation of self, nay, in aversion for self, and thus in absence from self, and so is in a state of receiving the Divine of the Lord. Hence it is that the Lord inflows with good into a humble and contrite heart.

He who places merit in goods, acknowledges and believes that all good is from self; because in the goods he does he regards self, and not the Lord... Therefore such a one despises others, and even condemns them...
That which is from self. Signified.
There is not anything which can subsist from itself...
The Lord acts from himself.
Under Merit, see this reference.
Reward,predicated of the Lord, = from himself.
For he who regards self as the end, and not as an end intermediate to good... is in evil.
Did good to the neighbour for the sake of self... AC 4226. AC 5807:end.
Lot of those who regard themselves alone in everything. AC 5395.

Almost every man of the Church believes that all the truth and good... are from self, although he says otherwise... (and) would say that he feels his life in himself, and that he thinks from himself, and wills from himself. AC 4319. AC 10330:2.
The Angels in the Middle Heaven are... in mutual love, which is such that one loves another more than himself; and, being such, they are in intelligence.
But in the First Heaven... they do not love others more than themselves, but as themselves.

The evil who had confirmed themselves in the opinion that they live from themselves, and consequently that whatever they think, will, and act is from themselves... now said they believed; but were told that to know is not to believe...
(Such) when they hear that love towards the neighbour does not begin from self, rejoice; whereas (such) sharply defend the idea that it does begin from self.

Believing from affection that he has no power of himself, nothing of intelligence and wisdom of himself, and nothing of good and truth of himself, he is gifted with power, intelligence of truth, and wisdom of good... (Such are signified by the poor and needy. AC 5008:2.)
Lot of those who believe that they understand... from themselves.
(Such are shown) by living experience that, of themselves, they are nothing but evil.
They want to enter Heaven from works in which is... the life of self. Signified.
Only loves those whom he regards as one with himself; thus loves them in himself, and himself in them, solely for the sake of the end of self. AC 4776. AC 4997:2. AC 5132:end.
Those who have studied nothing but the things of self and the world, have shut out all influx from Heaven...
The essence of charity is... the acknowledgement of self as being evil and falsity...

The naked, sick, and bound = those who acknowledge that there is nothing of good and truth ia themselves; that there is nothing but evil in themselves; and that there is nothing but falsity in themselves.
The natural man rejects whatever he regards as separated from self, and accepts whatever he regards as conjoined with self...
All evil is from themselves, that is, with themselves, from Hell.
That which is exterior never thinks from itself. (Explained.)
In adolescence, he begins to think from himself...
In saying that they do not act from themselves, but from others, they relate to the peritoneum, which also is such.
Heavenly freedom is... to will nothing from self... nay, to think nothing from self... They are in trouble and grief if permitted to think, or will, from themselves.
That man thinks nothing from himself... appears as hard to him who wants to think from himself...
Heaven and its joy begin in man when regard for self in the uses he does expires.
Those who relate to the membranes... are passive forces; for they act nothing from themselves, but from others.
Affection of good and truth not for the sake of self... is spiritual.
For man to become spiritual, it is necessary for his Natural... to be able to do nothing from itself. Explained.
Spirits (then) think that... if they cannot do good of themselves, nor believe truth of themselves, they should... await influx. They are permitted to (try it).
a. [end]. That man may be gifted with a heavenly proprium, and heavenly freedom, he must do good as of himself, and think truth as of himself...
That it is against the Divine law to claim it for themselves. Signified, Explained. AC 5758.

Spiritual theft is claiming for self the good and truth which are from the Lord. Treated of. No one can he admitted into Heaven until he acknowledges in heart that nothing of good and truth is from himself... and that whatever is from himself is nothing but evil. Explained.
A Subject thinks and speaks nothing from himself... AC 5986.
When left to self, he is seized with grief and anxiety...
Despair produces an effectual acknowledgement that nothing of truth and good is from themselves, and that, from themselves, they are damned...

The Angels are in the manifest perception (that the influxes of good and truth are not from themselves); and love nothing more than not to think and will from themselves, but from the Lord; whereas evil spirits are angry if told that they do not think and will from themselves...

Troops of such Spirits come from the world, and the influx from them with man is that he... should live for self and the world, and not for others, except in so far as they favour self and its pleasures.
For man, from himself, is in Hell.

Thought about recompense renders love impure; because they then think about themselves... how they may render themselves happy... Thus they turn love towards the neighbour into love towards self; and, in the same proportion joy and happiness... cannot be communicated to them; for they concentrate the influx of happiness... on self, and do not transmit it to others; and are thus like objects which... absorb the rays of light...
The Angels perceive sweetness from this: that they do not think and will from themselves, but from the Lord: hence they have tranquillity, peace, and happiness.
One who had instructed others that... man cannot think or will good from himself, when brought into a state in which he did not think and will from himself... said that he could not live so...
The evil are permitted to believe that all things are of their own prudence... and their successes incite them more because they ascribe them to themselves.
Those especially are prone to magic who... have trusted in themselves...
Those who cry to the Lord for themselves alone... He hears, but does not aid them.
For he who turns the ends to self, turns himself towards Hell; but he who turns the ends from self to the neighbour, turns himself towards Heaven.
Man, from himself, looks only downwards, that is, to the world... because, from himself, he is in evil and falsity.

AC 7368. The love of self reigns... when man does all things for the sake of himself and his... It is said for the sake of himself and his, because he with his, and his with him, make one... They regard themselves in him, and him in themselves.
(Inhabitants of Mars) said that from themselves, they are devils...

Man has been so created that he can look above self, and also... below self. To look above self is to look to the neighbour, one's country, the Church, and Heaven, especially to the Lord: to look below self is to look to the Earth, the world, and especially to self. AC 7815. Explained. AC 7816. AC 7817. AC 7818. AC 7820. AC 8604.
He who turns the good and truth inflowing from the Lord to self, sees self and the world before himself, and the Lord with His good and truth he does not see, because they are behind him.

To look above self is proper to man, but to look below self is proper to beasts; thus, in proportion as a man looks below self, he is a beast... and in proportion as he looks above self, he is a man...
Those in the genuine affection of charity and faith believe that they will nothing of good from themselves, and understand nothing of truth from themselves.
In temptations, man must combat as of himself, but still acknowledge and believe that it is of the Lord. Signified, Explained. AC 8969, Explained.
They who trust in themselves. Treated of.

Divine worship consists in the exaltation of the Lord relatively to self... Man is then in the state of receiving... the truth of faith and the good of charity... But if man exalts himself before the Lord, he closes the interiors of his mind...

Man can abstain from evils from himself; but he cannot receive good from himself. The reason man can abstain from evils from himself, is that the Lord continually inflows into the will of man with this conatus...
Man, from himself, is continually falling...
Those are not in the stream of Providence who trust in themselves alone, and attribute all things to themselves; for they are in the opposite. AC 8480.
The abuse of Divine good: that they want to procure it from themselves, for themselves. Signified, Explained.
They who trust in themselves continually induce evil on themselves...
For he who acts from truth, leads himself...
When man does good for the sake of self... he closes his interiors, and cannot be led... by the Lord; but is led by self... He who loves self more than the neighbour, leads himself... AC 8516:end.
If the man were then to lead himself, even by truth, he would dissipate the state of peace.

Spirits of Jupiter modestly replied that they suppose they can do good from themselves... saying that it is simpler to say so. It was given to reply that the Lord leaves those who live in simplicity and innocence to say so, provided they know that nothing of good comes from themselves, but from the Lord.
The faith which looks... to self and the world yields, because the man then fights from himself.
No one can know these (spiritual truths) from themselves. Explained.
(Man is) in a state of misery, because from himself he is wholly in evil and in Hell...
When man, in this freedom, from himself desists from evil, the affection of truth and good is insinuated.
All who, from themselves, that is, from the flesh, think about God, think about Him without any terminated idea...
Hence (the Angels) have the appearance that they act from themselves, but the perception that they do so from the Lord.
That the things of the Lord are not to be attributed to self. Signified, Explained.
He does truth and good (merely) to be rewarded, and therefore in the truth and good he does there is the idea of self...
Those who are in good... act from... the will, thus from themselves; for whatever is of the will with man is his proprium; for the esse of man's life is his will... AC 8990:2.
The Lord inspires good into the will, (which) appears to be from (the man) himself, thus from freedom.
Those in truths of faith only... are relatively servants, because they do not act from themselves; because they have no good in themselves from which to act, but outside themselves...

(A regenerate man) when he looks to the Lord, holds himself as nothing, and also the world; and, if he regards himself as anything, it is that he may be able to serve the Lord. Previously, he had been in the contrary: when he looked to himself, he held the Lord as nothing...
To make one hair white = to say that truth is truth from themselves; and to make one hair black = to say that falsity is falsity from themselves.
They who regard themselves and the world in the first place, cannot see what is just and good, because they are in the intuition of self and of gain.

He who binds and enkindles another to confirm his own truths, causes the other not to think and speak from himself, but from him; and when anyone thinks and speaks from another, the truths with him are disturbed, and yet he is not amended.
That all goods and truths are to be ascribed to the Lord, and not to self. Signified, Explained.
Innocence is to acknowledge at heart that of himself he wills nothing but evil, and perceives nothing but falsity. AC 9301:2. HH 278. HH 279.

When man is in externals... he is in such shade that he cannot apprehend otherwise than that externals inflow into internals, consequently that the eye sees and the ear hears from itself; and that their objects produce thoughts... and thus he can from himself believe in, and from himself love God.
If the use of life is solely for self and the world, this initiament of the new will is closed; and below it is formed a voluntary from the evils of the love of self and the world...
It is to be known that, from himself, man cannot approach the Lord...
These do not suffer themselves to be elevated; for they keep their intuition (or mental view) fixed to themselves and the world.
That man cannot of himself do good or think truth, but of the Lord, is evident from: a man cannot do anything unless it is given him from heaven (). Further Illustrated. AC 9981.
They who are illuminated of self... see falsity as truth, and evil as good.

They who are in goods and truths from the Lord, possess nothing of good and truth from themselves. Representation. Goods and truths from self... are signified by possessing gold, silver, and brass in their girdles, and by a scrip ... Two coats, shoes, and staves = truths and their powers from both the Lord and self...
They who believe that by the goods they do they merit Heaven, do goods from themselves...
None of the goods which men do from themselves are goods, because they do them for the sake of themselves...
Besides, man from himself is nothing but evil; thus to do good from self is to do it from evil. DP 277.
In this state, man is led through truth to good, thus partly by himself.
Lest there be the penalty of evil in doing good as of themselves. Signified, Explained.
It is said as of themselves, because the goods which man does he does as of himself: he perceives no otherwise until he is in faith from love. Explained.

So long as man believes that he does all things of himself, both goods and evils, so long the goods do not affect him, and the evils adhere to him... But so Ions as man is in such a state that he cannot perceive and feel the influx of goods from the Lord, so long he does goods as of himself, but still he ought to acknowledge and believe that it is of the Lord; and, when he does this, he is delivered from evils...

There are three plagues which follow those who attribute the truths and goods of faith and love to themselves... 1. That they cannot receive anything of the good of love and truth of faith. 2. That evils and falsities constantly pursue them. 3. That the truths and goods received from infancy perish. Signified.
In proportion as it is acknowledged that nothing of good and truth is from self, the love of self departs...
It does not matter if at first... the affection of truth is also for the sake of self and the world...
But still... man ought to think, will, and act as of himself...
For man then loves influx from the Lord, and is averse to operation from self.
Man looks outwards from himself... (and) when he looks from himself, he looks to Hell...
He that profaneth the Sabbath = to be led by self and one's own loves. Explained.
To cut wood = to operate good from self.
They then do not think from self; nor are affected with the Word from self, but from the Lord; hence no evil nor falsity of evil enters.

But these, when they read the Word, are not illustrated... what they see they see from themselves; and to see from themselves is to see falsities for truths; and if they see truths they falsify them by principles taken from themselves...
Not to make gods of what is molten = the worship of self.

Men have two states as to the things of the Church: some turn themselves to the Lord; some turn themselves to themselves and the world. The former receive influx from Him, and are in illustration... the latter are in no illustration...
To turn one's self to one's self, is to be turned by Hell; and, when this takes place, the things of the internal man are closed, lest the man should serve two masters.

When anyone is in the temple (the inhabitants of the Fourth Earth) say that he is not with himself... by which they mean that he is with God... for so far as he is with God he is not with himself, or in his own house...
Everyone doing work on the seventh day shall die = spiritual death for those who are led by themselves and their own loves, and not by the Lord. Explained.
(Priests) who attribute the honour to themselves souls... set honour and gain before the salvation of souls...
Everyone there... perceives that he wills and does nothing of good from himself... HH 9:end.

Spirits who have confirmed themselves in the faith that the good and truth they do are from themselves, or are appropriated to themselves as their own... are not received into Heaven: the Angels shun them...
Hypocrites are those who speak and do well, but regard themselves in every single thing...
The Angels have no power whatever from themselves... An Angel who believes that he has power from himself, becomes (utterly) weak.
He who lives a moral life for the sake of men, is led by self. HH 319:2.
Interiorly, they are worshippers of self and the world.
He who loves Divine truths for the sake of the glory of self, regards himself in Divine truths... and thus turns his sight... from the Lord to self; and thus is... not in the light of Heaven.
In Heaven the least is the greatest, and he is called the least who... wills to have no power or wisdom from self...
If the thought is turned to self and the honour of self, it becomes corporeal.

Man is let into his... hereditary evils whenever he regards self in the goods he does; for he looks from the goods to self; and not from self to the goods; and therefore in the goods he presents an image of self, and not any image of the Divine... There are evil Spirits... who are skilled in the art of letting upright ones into thoughts about self.
Spirits who had... set themselves before their uses.
Man ought to shun evil and do good as if of himself, yet with the acknowledgement that it is of the Lord. DLife 22. DLife 101, General article. Char 203, Explained.
That no one can do good which is good from himself. General article. DLife 17, illustrated. DLife 29.
In proportion as man shuns evils as sins, he does goods not from himself... General article.
Every man is such that he can shun evils as of himself from the Lord's power, if he implores it...

The man who fights against evils, cannot but fight as of himself; for he who does not do so as of himself, does not fight; but stands like an automaton... But still... it only appears to man as if he fights from himself; and the Lord wills that it should so appear... DLife 101, General article.
To act from freedom according to reason is to act from self... (but) as freedom and reason are in man from the Lord... it follows that he does not act from self, but as from self.
No one can act repentance except as of himself.
Still, the reaction (on the part of man) is as of himself.
God is... not existent from Himself, but in Himself... DLW 44. DLW 76.
Thus reaction becomes of action, and man acts with God as of himself.
For that which is in itself, is the Esse itself from which all things are...
An Angel perceives no otherwise than that he is in love and wisdom of himself... Unless he so perceived, there would be no conjunction (with the Lord).
Some opine that Adam... could love God of himself...
From these (faculties) comes the appearance that man thinks, wills, speaks, and acts as from himself.
As man feels as if he does from himself whatever he does from the natural man, he ought as from himself to remove evils...
The (celestial) Angels... call it slavery to be led by self. Explained.
No one can receive good and truth from the Lord unless it appears to him that he perceives them as of himself.

So far as man acknowledges (that goods are of the Lord with man) so far the Lord grants that good should appear to man as his, that is, that it should appear to man that he has charity as of himself, that he has faith as of himself, that he does good and understands truth, thus is wise, as of himself. From which an enlightened man can see how strong is the appearance in which the Lord wills man to be...
That... man can be regenerated in so far as... he can be brought to acknowledge that all the truth and good which he thinks and does are from the Lord, and not from himself. General article.
Hence man wills and understands nothing from himself, but only as from himself.
It is not truth and good in itself...

(By this Reciprocal on the part of man) good and truth appear to him as from himself, and as his, exactly as if they were his: there is no difference... except that man ought to acknowledge that he does not do good and think truth from himself, but from the Lord...
The difference between those who believe all good to be from the Lord, and those who believe good to be from themselves. From experience.
It is a law of the Divine Providence that man should as from himself remove evils as sins in the external man... General article. DP 118.
(Necessity of the appearance that man does good, etc. as from himself.) DP 210, General article. AR 541. CL 132:6. CL 134:5. AE 802:5.
It is a law of the Divine Providence that man be led and taught by the Lord from the Word... in all appearance as of himself. General article. DP 174, Explained.

As man disposes the externals, so the Lord disposes the internals; thus in one way if man disposes the externals of himself, and in another way if he disposes them from the Lord, and at the same time as of himself.
He who attributes the honour of his office to himself, appears (there) inverted.
A reasoner wants to see Divine things from himself; and that which man sees from himself is evil.
When a man regards himself in his dignities...
The difference is that one is interiorly in the Lord, and exteriorly as it were in self; and the other is interiorly in self, and exteriorly as it were in the Lord...
(Arguments of) every worshipper of self and of nature against the Divine Providence. Explained. DP 250. DP 251. DP 252.
That no one can think from himself...
That no one in Hell thinks from himself, but from others around himself, nor these from themselves, but also from others... From experience.

Leibnitz was thus convinced that no one thinks from himself, but from others; and that neither do these think from themselves; but all from influx from Heaven; and Heaven from influx from the Lord. DP 294.
As man... wants to think from himself... he cannot reject the fault [of evil] from himself... Whereas if he does not love (to think from himself), he sets himself loose from connection with them...
Whatever, therefore, man believes that he does from himself, is said to be done from the man...
Man is thereby led away from evil; not by himself, but by the Lord. Explained.
The difference between these two kinds of intelligence is like that between what is believed to be in itself, and that which is believed not to be in itself, but still as in itself.
From Own prudence man persuades himself, and confirms with himself, that all good and truth is from himself, and in himself; in like manner all evil and falsity. Explained.

It is from a law of the Divine Providence that man should think as from himself, and should act prudently as from himself; but should acknowledge that it is from the Lord. It follows that he who (does this) is a man; but not he who confirms with himself that everything he thinks and acts is from himself...
Still, man thinks as from himself, although he does so from Hell...

(Thus) man can think evil and falsity as from himself; and can also think that this or that is evil and false; consequently that it is only an appearance that it is from himself... The human itself is to think from the Truth; and this is the Truth: that man does not think from himself; but to think is given him by the Lord, in all appearance as from himself.
Everyone in Hell supposes that he thinks from himself.
They know that they can avail nothing from themselves. Signified.
Laodicea = those in the Church who believe alternately from themselves and from the Word; and thus profane holy things.

(Thus) man can reform and regenerate himself as of himself, provided he at heart acknowledges that it is from the Lord... Man must do both as of himself; but the as of himself is from the Lord... In a word, do it from yourselves, and believe that it is from the Lord; and thus you will do it as of yourselves.

The Englishmen asked whether to do as of himself has been implanted in man from creation. The Angel replied, It has not been implanted, because to do of self is of God alone; but it is continually given, that is, continually adjoined; and then, in proportion as man does good and believes truth, as of himself, he is an Angel of Heaven; and in proportion as he does evil and thence believes falsity, which also is as of himself, he is an Angel of Hell... Everyone becomes guilty who believes that he does of himself, whether it is good, or evil; but he does not become guilty who believes that he does as of himself.
When we are acting from the Word, we cannot say, I am doing this from myself.
All those do goods from themselves who do not shun evils as sins.
Man can, from himself, reject evil; but not its concupiscences...
Therefore, no Angel, or man, can produce from himself anything good or true, which in itself is good and true.
I longed to know how man can do good from God, and yet as of himself. AR 875:10, Fully Explained. TCR 461:2.
The ability to desist from evil is given by the Lord to every man, because He gives him to will and understand as of himself...
This is done by man as of himself, because he does not feel that he does anything from the Lord.
The Divine Esse is the Divine Esse in itself, not from itself; because from itself implies an Esse in itself a quo... TCR 21.

The likeness of God is the full appearance as if love and wisdom were in man... for man feels... that he loves of himself, and is wise of himself, or that he wills good and understands truth of himself; when yet [he does these things] not a whit of himself, but of God. God alone loves of Himself, and is wise of Himself...
The tree of the knowledge of good and evil = man believing that he lives from himself, and not from God... CL 444:4.
The Lord alone, when in the world, was wise from Himself, and did good from Himself.

The highest region in man has been turned upwards to God; the middle one outwards to the world; and the lowest one downwards to self; and, because this last has been turned downwards, man thinks as of himself...

The two Angels asked. How could man turn himself from God, and turn to himself, when yet man cannot will, think, or do anything except from God... I replied, Man has been created so that all he wills, thinks, and does appears to him as in himself, and thus from himself. Without this appearance, man would not be man... But if from this appearance, he induces on himself the belief that he wills, thinks, and does good from himself, and not from the Lord in all appearance as from himself, he turns good into evil with himself, and thus makes in himself the origin of evil. This was the sin of Adam. Further explained.
Whatever man believes that he does of himself, he appropriates to himself, (whether good, or evil).

Let everyone beware how he persuades himself that he lives from himself, or that he is wise, believes, loves, perceives truth, and wills and does good from himself; for (in the same proportion) he casts down his mind... to the earth, and... becomes natural, sensuous, and corporeal. Explained. TCR 69:2.
This man must do of himself, but acknowledge that it is from God.
Man from himself is merely passive; but... from the perpetual influx of life from the Lord, it appears to man as if he were active from himself...

Two canons for the New Church. 1. No one can shun evils as sins, and do goods which are goods before God, of himself; but, in proportion as anyone shuns evils as sins, he does goods not from himself, but from the Lord. II. Man ought to shun evils as sins, and fight against them, as of himself... TCR 596:2.
In proportion as man does not prepare himself, he removes the Lord from himself, and does all things himself, from himself; and that which man himself does from himself has no life in itself.
It has been provided... that man should feel in himself as his own the things which inflow from without, and thence should produce them from himself as his own...
There is a mutual conjunction of the Lord and man... for the Lord acts, and man receives action from Him, and operates as of himself, nay, from himself from the Lord... TCR 576, Explained.
Man becomes a hypocrite when he thinks much about himself, and sets himself before others...

Man cannot possibly act from himself from spiritual justice and fidelity; for every man derives from his parents [the nature] that he does what is good and just for the sake of self and the world... and therefore he who worships the Lord, and acts from Him when from himself, alone acquires spiritual charity.

As man does nothing of good, unless it appears to him as if ability, will, and action were of himself, therefore this has been given him; and, when he does it from freedom as of himself, it is imputed to him...
Free will is that man can will, do, think, and speak in all appearance as of himself... TCR 504:7.
On the life of those who are wise from themselves.
The wonder of the Spirits when I said that I can do nothing from myself... I told them that the things done from me were not done by me, but through me, so that I seemed to myself to do them...
A Spirit who defended himself by saying that he did nothing of himself.
Punishment of a Spirit who desired to do everything from himself, as if he were alone.
a. On the vastation of those who trust in themselves. SE 1386. SE 1414.

Spirits were told not to do anything from themselves; thus without reflection on themselves; but this does not mean to become passive. Whenever they attempt anything from themselves, it is nothing, except sin. SE 1629. SE 1630. SE 1637.
They supposed things to be done by themselves which were done by others.
That he who knows nothing from himself begins to be wise...
That neither man nor Spirit can do the least thing from self, although to themselves, all things seem to be from themselves. SE 2325. SE 2428. SE 2464. From experience. SE 2470.
Those who study themselves only... SE 2566. SE 2772.
Those in faith do not speak from themselves...
The sweetness of not thinking from self. Explained.
Indignant that they can do nothing from themselves. SE 2966.
On one who supposed he could do good from himself.
This offspring of the Most Ancient Church supposed that they could do good of themselves.
Man cannot know otherwise than that [he acts] from himself. Explained.
Nothing is from itself. Explained.

When anyone there thinks and speaks within the sphere of generals, it is as if from himself... But when he thinks and speaks what does not pertain so to the general sphere, it is as if not from himself...
Punishment of those who suppose they act from themselves. Explained.
One who was constantly thinking about himself... hence a sphere of self-honour.
Man first does good from the end of self or the world... These ends are gradually removed by the Lord.
On those who are in offices and dignity, and think only about themselves.

Evil Spirits... know how to lead all those who think about themselves, and also do lead them wherever they want... in proportion as they can turn their thoughts upon themselves. But those who do not [direct their thoughts] to self, but to others whom they esteem more worthy than themselves, most especially if to the Lord, they cannot move. When man is thinking about self, he is in the love of self... if he sets himself above others... Evil Spirits know how... to turn the thoughts of another Spirit upon himself, and so to lead him... Explained. SE 5464, Explained.
The influx of good from the Lord effects nothing unless man does good as of himself, Explained. SE 6050.
They do not think within themselves, but without themselves, (that is), from the memory only.
They apprehend all things from themselves... and the things man apprehends from himself (alone) are false, because he thinks in darkness.
The acknowledgement that they know nothing from themselves. Signified, Explained.
The Lord wills that man should from himself abstain from evils and do goods...
Two states of man's thoughts... one when he thinks about truths from self... his mind then falls into the light of the world...
(Fascinating effect of self-confidence upon others.) Signified, Explained.
(This implies) that if man could fulfil the law from himself, he would be saved, which is false.
Whatever man does from the external (alone), he does from himself. Signified.
He abstains from self, and not from the Lord.
If man does and speaks what is good, true, sincere, and just, for the sake of self and the world, he does and speaks these things from self... and they are all evil... AE 797:4.

As the Lord is continually present... man has the faculty of desisting from evils as of himself; this has been given to every man. Hence, as man of himself can close Heaven, he can of himself open it, provided that when he thinks and wills to desist from evils, he looks to the Lord...
That faith has been given as the means of Salvation, because man cannot do good of himself. Explained.

That man can (keep these commandments) of himself, is known... but still he cannot desist from these sins from himself, but from God; but, when he desists from them from God, the man is still thinking that he wills to desist from them because they are sins; thus he desists from them as of himself... Then, as he calls adultery sin, he lives in chastity and loves it, and this also as of himself; and, as he calls theft sin, he lives in sincerity and loves it, and this also as of himself; as he calls murder sin, he lives in charity and loves it, and this as of himself; as he calls false witness sin, he lives in truth and justice, and loves them, and this as of himself; and, although he lives and loves these things as of himself, still he lives and loves them from God; for whatever man does as from himself from chastity itself, from sincerity itself, from charity itself, and from Truth and justice itself, he does from God, and thence they are good. In a word, all things whatever which man does from these things as from himself, evils being removed, are from God, and are good...
No one can follow the Lord of himself. Explained.

Unless it appeared to man that he follows the Lord as of himself... there would be no appropriation and conjunction, and hence no reformation and regeneration; for everything enters man, and is as his, which he receives from freedom, that is, as from himself... But still man ought to believe, as the Thing is in itself, that he does not do it from himself, but from the Lord; and therefore it is not said that he must do it of himself, but as of himself. The reason it is so, is also that man does not perceive the Lord's operation into his will and thence into his thought... and he therefore supposes that whatever he wills and thinks, he wills and thinks of himself; and therefore he cannot know otherwise than that he does this of himself, when yet all the good inflows... and, as he knows this from doctrine... he ought to believe that he does not do good of himself, although he does it as of himself. This is taught by the Lord in ; . AE 911:17. AE 946:end.
The mistake of supposing that Angels were so created that they could do good of themselves.
If man does not fight against them as of himself, evils are not separated.

Still, man ought to shun evils as of himself; for that which man does as of himself, becomes his, and is appropriated to him as his own; but that which he does not do as of himself, never becomes his, or is appropriated to him. That which comes from the Lord to man must be received by man, and it cannot be received except with him conscious, that is, as of himself. This reciprocal is necessary for reformation.
Man's thinking that he will shun evil and do good as of himself is not caused by man, but by the Lord... for the sake of what is reciprocal...
And this also as of themselves, although from Hell.
All who see God as a Man, see Him from the Lord; all others see Him from themselves; and those who see Him from themselves, do not see Him.
Life from itself cannot be said, because from itself involves an origin.
As man cannot (do anything) from himself... why is not every man saved? Explained.
Loves these apparently from himself, but actually of the Lord... Loves these apparently from himself, but actually from Hell.

Some Angels... not comprehending that evil and falsity are from Hell... were brought into infernal Societies... in each of which they thought as the devils there did... They were told to think from themselves, thus differently; but replied that they could not... AE 1148:4.
Man... does not know that... the faculty of acting as of himself, is from the influx of life from the Lord into his inmost...
From himself, man is constantly acting against order...
In order to be drawn out of Hell... it is necessary for man to resist it... as of himself. If he does not resist it as of himself, he remains in Hell, and Hell in him, to eternity. From experience.
In the whole Spiritual World there is not a single case of anyone's having been removed from evils, except through combat, or resistance, as of himself.
The Lord does not teach man truths immediately... for otherwise he would not act as from himself. (Explained.)
Neither had Adam freedom from himself, but as from himself.
They have a continual intuition upon self...
To act and think as of himself in spiritual things, is the image of God in man, and is given perpetually by the Lord.
The likeness of God... is that man can live, that is, will, etc., in all appearance as of himself...
